evidence_items.content: Quelhas and Pinto describe bias updating as a widespread adaptation procedure for allowing inference models to follow time-varying features of a real process.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Establishes bias updating as an established output-correction family directly within the RQ boundary.

evidence_items.content: In the statistical setting analyzed by Quelhas and Pinto, bias-updated inferences were unbiased but had 100% larger variance than estimates without bias updating; the authors therefore suggest weighting the bias update to balance benefits and penalties.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Captures a documented variance trade-off and the rationale for weighted rather than full correction.

evidence_items.content: Shardt and Huang analyze a soft-sensor bias update term for the ideal open-loop case, measurement delay, multirate sampling, and the combination of delay and multirate sampling, and provide tuning rules aimed at tracking the quality variable under slow or drifting disturbances.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Shows that delay and sparse/multirate quality measurements can be designed into bias correction rather than requiring base-model retraining.

evidence_items.content: The open-loop bias-update study reports simulation and experimental validation of its tuning rules, indicating that delay and measurement frequency are explicit design conditions rather than details that can be ignored.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Supports design-condition requirements for applying a bias updater to delayed laboratory quality measurements.

evidence_items.content: Sangoi et al. propose Bayesian automatic bias updating using online process-variable measurements and sporadic laboratory measurements of the critical variable; the method continuously monitors the mean and standard deviation of prediction error and adapts the bias without operational parameter adjustment.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Provides a self-adaptive statistical bias estimator suitable when ground-truth quality is sporadic.

evidence_items.content: For simulated examples of a continuous styrene-butadiene-rubber process, the Bayesian bias-updating method produced estimates similar to classical approaches after their parameter tuning, while the Bayesian bias showed lower variability.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Provides continuous-process evaluation and a variability comparison for Bayesian versus classical bias updating.

evidence_items.content: Du, Guan, and Qian construct a static LS-SVM soft sensor and use an ARMA model to dynamically estimate its prediction error; that estimated error is added as a dynamic correction to the static model output.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Establishes residual time-series modeling as a correction layer outside a fixed predictor.

evidence_items.content: In an ethylene-distillation simulation for ethane concentration, the LSSVM-ARMA error-compensation approach was reported to have better tracking and generalization than using the LSSVM model alone.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Provides process-domain evidence that dynamic residual correction can outperform an uncorrected static predictor.

evidence_items.content: Wu and Luo distinguish soft-sensor output calibration from model self-adjustment and describe output calibration as an operationally simpler, lower-cost alternative when operating conditions do not change greatly.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Directly supports the RQ distinction between output correction and base-model adaptation and states an applicability limit.

evidence_items.content: Wu and Luo propose multirate Kalman-filter data fusion to calibrate soft-sensor model estimates using process measurements sampled at different rates.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Establishes Kalman/data-fusion calibration as a no-base-retraining correction architecture.

evidence_items.content: Their simulations and laboratory-scale experiment indicate that multirate Kalman-filter calibration can improve soft-estimation accuracy and reliability when essential process dynamics are included in the filter model and filter parameters are properly tuned.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Captures both evidence of benefit and the requirement for adequate dynamics and tuning.

evidence_items.content: Klimchenko et al. replace a purely sample-based bias update with a predictive correction layer that models historical prediction errors; their implementation uses an ARMA predictive filter in the compensator so future model error can be predicted and added to the soft-sensor output.
evidence_items.source_locator: §1 Introduction; §2.3 Summary of the Proposed Approach
evidence_items.selection_reason: Provides a predictive-residual correction architecture that leaves the process predictor separate from the error model.

evidence_items.content: The predictive-error filter is stated to be suitable when the error sequence is stationary or close to stationary, or can be transformed to such a process; the authors also require performance checking on a test sample not used to fit the correction model.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Defines key applicability and validation conditions for an error-prediction corrector.

evidence_items.content: On the industrial reactive-distillation dataset, the predictive-error filter reduced MSE for three output variables by 32%, 67%, and 9.5% relative to a moving-window adaptive-bias method; the authors note that the filters used do not handle serious disturbances or outliers well.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Provides industrial-data comparison plus a documented failure mode for residual-prediction correction.

evidence_items.content: Qian et al. report that applying different nonlinear filters to correct errors of the same data-driven composition soft sensor led to different dynamic trade-offs in a Kaibel dividing-wall column: EKF showed oscillations, PF retained steady-state offsets, and UKF gave stable behavior without those two observed issues in that application.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Demonstrates that correction-filter choice can change dynamic behavior and that there is no process-independent universal filter choice.

evidence_items.content: Dong et al. structure their Double Gaussian Bayesian Network as an offline prediction model plus a calibration model; the prediction model supplies initial estimates, while the calibration model learns from prediction errors to improve those estimates.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Provides direct evidence for a frozen/offline predictor plus a separate adaptive calibration layer.

evidence_items.content: The authors distinguish bias correction from parameter correction and note that bias correction is easy to implement but may become inadequate under large working-condition changes; their ADGBN therefore incrementally updates the auxiliary calibration model and uses a dynamic variable window to decide adaptive updates.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Defines an intermediate correction-layer adaptation strategy and states when simple bias correction may be insufficient.
